hints: Focus on what the word giant means, a never-ending network of atoms joined by covalent bonds versus separate little molecules.
Think about diamond as a 3D tetrahedral network and graphite as endless hexagonal layers, both continuing in all directions.
Remember that buckminsterfullerene is a closed cage of 60 carbons that exists as a discrete molecule, so decide which two are truly giant.
walkthrough:
**Recall what giant molecular means**

Think of it as giant covalent. Millions of atoms joined by strong covalent bonds in one continuous lattice, not separate molecules.

Rule to use:
$$\text{giant covalent = continuous network, very high melting point}$$

**Check diamond and graphite**

Diamond has every carbon tetrahedrally bonded to four others in a 3D network. Graphite has every carbon bonded to three others in endless hexagonal layers with delocalised electrons between layers.

Structures:
$$\text{diamond: C bonded to 4 C, tetrahedral network}$$
$$\text{graphite: C bonded to 3 C, layered hexagonal network}$$

**Check buckminsterfullerene**

This is $\text{C}_{60}$, a hollow football-shaped cage. Each cage is a separate simple molecule, with only weak van der Waals forces between cages.

Key contrast:
$$\text{C}_{60} \text{ : simple molecular, not giant}$$

**Conclude the correct combination**

Only 2 and 3 form continuous giant networks. Statement 1 does not, so the answer is 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would include all three. Buckminsterfullerene ($\text{C}_{60}$) is not giant, it is simple molecular with discrete cages and low melting point compared to diamond and graphite.
options.B: Incorrect. This would pair buckminsterfullerene with diamond only. It wrongly includes 1 and wrongly leaves out graphite, which is definitely a giant layered structure.
options.C: Correct. Diamond (3D tetrahedral network) and graphite (2D hexagonal layers extending indefinitely) are both giant molecular structures, while buckminsterfullerene is a simple molecular fullerene.
options.D: Incorrect. This would select buckminsterfullerene alone. That is the opposite of the truth, as $\text{C}_{60}$ exists as separate molecules held by weak intermolecular forces, not a giant lattice.
